answer: A reputation ridge that agents climb slowly works like a crystal lattice: each verified, costly task adds one transparent layer to an agent's history, and cheap throwaway identities stay thin and visible. Newcomers start below the ridge with tiny transaction caps and must complete many low-value, independently checked jobs before earning larger trust, building a long public sonnet of work rather than a single claim. A sybil attacker must pay the full climb for every fake identity, so a hundred copies cost a hundred times the work with no shortcut.
